clue.text: Dedicated, unite to protect man with skill after awkward situation

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so the first word wraps around the rest
after sends the man with skill behind the awkward situation in the order

blocks.note: to wed is to unite in marriage
being in a hole is being in a tight spot
the male pronoun
art as in craft or knack

explanation.surface: A devoted person getting married to shelter a talented man after some trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unite' looks like part of the definition beside 'Dedicated', but the comma cuts it off: it is the outer piece of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wholehearted gives full, sincere commitment, which is what being dedicated means.

clue.text: Each hint, fraught with meaning, demanding a lot of attention

indicators.note: fraught suggests tension and upset, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Every clue is loaded with significance, which makes the puzzle hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fraught with meaning' reads as one stock phrase, but 'with' only joins: all fifteen letters of 'Each hint' and 'meaning' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-maintenance person or thing needs constant care and effort, the idiom for something needing much attention.

clue.text: Release defamatory statement mostly connected with class

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: libel is a written defamation
rate as in first-rate, a grade or class

explanation.surface: Publishing a slanderous remark about social class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' suggests the social sort, but here it is a grade, as in first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate is to set free, a direct verb synonym for release.

clue.text: Try and find out

blocks.note: first meaning: to judge a case in court, as a judge does
second meaning: to learn of news

explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like attempt, but here it is the legal sense of hearing a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge hears a case when trying it, and to hear something is also to learn of it.

clue.text: Run, notice little, then rest, shattered

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: an advertisement, a public notice
mini means small
the word rest rearranged

explanation.surface: An exhausted person who barely noticed anything and now needs a lie-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shattered' reads as tired, but it breaks up the word 'rest'.
explanation.definitionFit: Administering a business means managing its affairs, the sense in which a manager runs a company.

clue.text: Hero of comic books in colour, popular

blocks.note: a tint is a shade of colour
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A cartoon hero printed in bright colours who is widely liked.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintin is the young reporter starring in Hergé's Belgian comic-book series.

clue.text: Confused record about mob led astray

indicators.note: led astray means taken off course, so these letters wander out of order

blocks.note: a gramophone record
these words rearranged with the next
part of the same rearrangement

explanation.surface: A muddled record about a gang being misled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container signal but is part of the fodder: 'about mob led' is rearranged after DISC.
explanation.definitionFit: Discombobulated is a jocular word meaning disconcerted or thrown into confusion.

clue.text: Circuit most important in computer

blocks.note: a lap is one circuit of a track
top means foremost

explanation.surface: The most important circuit inside a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circuit' suggests electronics, but it is a lap of a track.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a portable computer, so it is a specific example of the defined device.

clue.text: Road made of stone skirting bay?

indicators.note: skirting means running around the edge, so the first part goes on both sides

blocks.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
the bay is a laurel tree

explanation.surface: A coastal road built of stone running round a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'bay' is not a stretch of coast but the bay tree. A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a public road in a town, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Time filled by learner with bluster, no good in area of maths

indicators.note: being filled by something means holding it inside, so the learner goes within
no good tells us to remove the letter that stands for good

blocks.note: an age is a period of time
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
to brag is to boast or bluster

explanation.surface: A student blustering through a long time with no good result in maths.
explanation.walkthrough: G is the usual abbreviation for good; 'in' merely joins the wordplay to 'area of maths'.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is the branch of mathematics using letters and symbols for numbers.

clue.text: Dislike group's attitude

blocks.note: to mind something is to object to it
a set is a group; the 's joins it on

explanation.surface: Resentment as the collective outlook of a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a fixed way of thinking, essentially an outlook or attitude.

clue.text: Tone from doctor interrupting bore

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: to tire someone is to bore them
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A medic's voice cutting into a dull talker.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the distinctive quality or colour of a sound, its tone.

clue.text: Remedy not available back before point in match

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the abbreviation runs the other way
in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation n/a
a dot is a point
a tie is a cup match

explanation.surface: A cure that can't be had again before the decisive point of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point in match' looks like a sporting term such as match point; in Britain a tie is a knockout cup fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote counteracts a poison, so it is a cure or remedy.

clue.text: Editor upset about lots of sheets and cover showing unreal scene

indicators.note: upset means overturned, which in a down clue turns the word upside down
about means around, so the reversed editor surrounds what follows

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation
a ream is 500 sheets of paper
a cap covers a head or bottle

explanation.surface: An upset editor surrounded by paperwork, looking at a fantastical picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamscape is a surreal, dreamlike landscape or picture, an unreal scene.

clue.text: Implement used for decorating different parts in hub

indicators.note: different means changed, so these letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A decorating tool with assorted components fitted into a central hub.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorators apply paint with this tool, so the definition describes its use.

clue.text: Encourage a prediction

blocks.note: taken as written
a bet is a forecast with stakes

explanation.surface: Urging someone on with a forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or incite someone, typically in wrongdoing, a synonym of encourage.

clue.text: Indignation led by celebrity, not a newcomer

indicators.note: not a tells us to drop one letter a from the celebrity word
led by puts the celebrity in front of the indignation

blocks.note: a star is a famous person
anger is indignation

explanation.surface: Outrage stirred up by a famous figure, rather than by someone new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a newcomer' looks like one phrase, but 'not a' deletes a letter from STAR and 'newcomer' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stranger is someone unfamiliar who has newly arrived, an outsider.

clue.text: Biblical book in reality omitting tons

indicators.note: omitting means leaving out, so one letter is removed

blocks.note: truth is what is real
t is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: A book of scripture that leaves out tons of reality.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a book of the Old Testament telling the story of Ruth the Moabite.

clue.text: Break made by part of posse certainly going north

indicators.note: part of tells us the letters sit inside the following words
in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A sheriff's band definitely taking a pause before riding north.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a break or adjournment, as between school lessons or parliamentary sittings.

clue.text: Unconvincing new chart pitifully bad

blocks.note: a lame excuse is unconvincing
n is the abbreviation for new
a table is a chart of data

explanation.surface: A weak, freshly drawn graph that is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitifully' looks like it qualifies 'chart', but 'pitifully bad' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamentable means deplorably poor, deserving regret, so pitifully bad fits.

clue.text: Wield overwhelming power in authority

indicators.note: overwhelming suggests engulfing something, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: to exert influence is to wield it
p is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Using crushing force in a position of command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Authority' sounds like official power, but here it means a specialist, someone who is an authority on a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: An authority on a subject is a recognised specialist, which is what an expert is.

clue.text: Rubbish layer rising and rising? Not half

indicators.note: the first rising, in a down clue, means reading upwards, so backwards
not half means only half of the preceding word is kept

blocks.note: a bed is a layer, as of rock
the second rising, taken as written

explanation.surface: Waste piling up higher and higher, though only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'rising' does two jobs: first it reverses BED, then it is itself cut to its first half, RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered rubbish or the broken remains of something.

clue.text: Have a chat, or the opposite

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to talk with someone
second meaning: a noun, the reverse of something

explanation.walkthrough: 'Or the opposite' seems to invite a word for falling silent, but it is a second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to talk informally; the noun, stressed on its first syllable, means the reverse or contrary.

clue.text: Belt needing work after partition

indicators.note: after sends the work piece behind the partition piece in the order

blocks.note: a wall divides a space
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A trouser belt that needs mending after a room is divided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt' looks like a noun, but it is a verb meaning hit hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To wallop is to strike hard, the same as the slang verb belt.

clue.text: Lose control suddenly following impudent talk

blocks.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
lip is cheek or back-talk

explanation.surface: Snapping in anger after hearing some cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like it means after, but it gives F, placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: To flip, or flip one's lid, is informal for suddenly losing one's temper.

clue.text: Warbled tune about drink

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for a tune runs backwards

blocks.note: warbled means sang
an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A singer crooning a song about a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine, fruit and soda, a type of drink.

clue.text: Type of barge that's less dark

blocks.note: first meaning: a flat-bottomed boat for unloading ships
second meaning: comparative of light, brighter

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it sounds like a paler barge; the two parts are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flat-bottomed boat for ferrying cargo; also the comparative adjective meaning paler or brighter.

clue.text: Musical film moving at a rare speed

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so these letters change places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A movie musical that rushes along unusually fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' seems to describe the film as touching, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter Parade is the 1948 Hollywood musical starring Fred Astaire and Judy Garland, with Irving Berlin songs.
